name: Mathematics
description: CXC CSEC Mathematics - Complete curriculum covering Number Concepts, Algebra, Geometry, Trigonometry, Statistics, and more

studyGuide.passStrategy: Master each topic's must-know ideas, work through examples, and complete practice questions before moving on.
studyGuide.masteryStrategy: For 100% preparation, explain every method aloud, practise unfamiliar variations, and complete timed mixed-topic questions.
studyGuide.notePrompt: For each topic, write the rule, one fully worked example, and one mistake to avoid.

units.title: Number Concepts
units.description: Understanding different types of numbers and operations
learningObjectives: Perform operations with integers, fractions, and decimals
Convert between fractions, decimals, and percentages
Apply ratio and proportion in real-world contexts

topics.title: Number Systems
topics.summary: Understanding different types of numbers and their properties
mustKnow: Rational numbers can be written as fractions
Irrational numbers cannot be written as simple fractions

keyTerms.definition: A whole number that can be positive, negative, or zero
Any number that can be expressed as p/q where q ≠ 0
A number that cannot be expressed as a simple fraction

examples.question: Classify -3, 0, 1/2, √2, and π
examples.answer: -3 is an integer, 0 is a whole number, 1/2 is rational, √2 and π are irrational
examples.explanation: Integers include negatives, whole numbers start at 0, rationals are fractions, irrationals cannot be fractions

commonMistakes: Confusing whole numbers with natural numbers
Forgetting that zero is a whole number but not a natural number
examTips: Always simplify fractions to lowest terms
Show all working when converting between number types

questions.question: Which of the following is an irrational number?
questions.explanation: √2 cannot be expressed as a simple fraction, making it irrational

topics.title: Integers
topics.summary: Working with positive and negative whole numbers
mustKnow: Integers include positive and negative whole numbers
Adding integers with same sign: add and keep sign
Adding integers with different signs: subtract and keep sign of larger
Multiplying/dividing integers: same signs positive, different signs negative

keyTerms.definition: Whole number that can be positive, negative, or zero
Distance from zero on number line

examples.question: Calculate: -5 + 3
examples.explanation: Different signs: subtract 5 - 3 = 2, keep sign of larger (negative)

examples.question: Calculate: (-4) × (-3)
examples.explanation: Same signs (both negative): result is positive

examTips: Use a number line for addition and subtraction

questions.question: Calculate: (-6) + (-4)
questions.explanation: Same signs: add 6 + 4 = 10, keep negative sign

topics.title: Fractions
mustKnow: Fraction represents part of a whole

topics.title: Decimals
topics.summary: Understanding and operating with decimal numbers
mustKnow: Decimals represent parts of a whole

topics.title: Ratio
mustKnow: Ratio compares two or more quantities

topics.title: Proportion
mustKnow: Direct proportion: as one increases, other increases
Inverse proportion: as one increases, other decreases

examples.question: If 5 books cost $25, how much do 8 books cost?

formulas: Inverse proportion: a × b = c × d

questions.question: If 6 workers take 8 days, how long will 4 workers take?

topics.title: Approximation

examples.question: Round 3.456 to 2 decimal places
examples.explanation: Third decimal is 6, so round up

examTips: Look at the digit after the required place

examples.question: How many significant figures in 0.00345?
examples.explanation: Leading zeros don't count, 345 are significant

examples.question: Round 4567 to 2 significant figures
examples.explanation: First two digits 45, next is 6 so round up

questions.question: How many significant figures are in 0.00520?
